textbook: Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE DNA DOUBLE HELIX molecule — two long antiparallel molecular strands twisted around a common vertical axis, centred in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space around it so labels can attach later, oriented with its long axis roughly vertical, showing at least 3 full helical turns from top to bottom. Fill the whole square edge-to-edge on a neutral dark-charcoal background with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox. Match a refined educational plate: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (not heavy black strokes), gentle soft shading, each structure its own distinct soft colour fill. CRITICAL HANDEDNESS: the helix MUST be RIGHT-HANDED — with the axis vertical, both backbone ribbons twist UPWARD AND TO THE RIGHT as they ascend, the same visual sense as a standard right-hand screw thread or a spiral staircase that turns clockwise as you climb it looking up. CONCRETE TEST: at every point where the two ribbons cross over one another, the ribbon drawn UNBROKEN AND ON TOP (nearer the viewer) must run diagonally from LOWER-LEFT to UPPER-RIGHT through that crossing, like a forward slash '/' — never from lower-right to upper-left. The ribbon that is interrupted/behind at that same crossing runs the opposite diagonal, like a backslash. Check every single crossing against this forward-slash rule before finalizing; a backslash front-strand at any crossing means the helix is wrongly mirrored (left-handed) and must be corrected. STRUCTURE: two ribbon-like backbones spiral around the axis — one backbone a cool slate blue-grey (#7FA0B8), the other a warm tan (#C9A876), deliberately different tones so the two antiparallel strands read as distinct rails, not a single mirrored ribbon. Between the two backbones, render flat paired rungs (base pairs) stacked perpendicular to the axis like the rungs of a spiral ladder — most rungs a mix of two rung types: some rungs green-paired-with-orange (adenine-thymine, drawn with exactly TWO short connecting cross-lines/bonds between them), others gold-paired-with-blue (guanine-cytosine, drawn with exactly THREE short connecting cross-lines/bonds) — vary the two rung types along the length so both are clearly visible at least a few times each. CRITICAL GROOVE ASYMMETRY: because the two backbone ribbons are not evenly spaced around the axis, the gaps between successive turns must be UNEQUAL — like a zipper with alternating long and short gaps, or piano keys of two different widths — one gap clearly WIDE (the major groove, roughly TWICE as wide) and the very next gap clearly NARROW (the minor groove), alternating regularly all the way up the helix. The wide and narrow grooves must be obviously, measurably different in width at a glance — never symmetric, never equal, never a uniform evenly-spaced ladder. Concretely: the repeating eye-shaped openings between crossings must alternate tall-and-wide, then short-and-narrow, then tall-and-wide again — like alternating long and short zipper teeth — NEVER a uniform row of identically-sized eye shapes. PRECISE MECHANISM for the asymmetry: do NOT place the two backbone ribbons exactly opposite each other (180 degrees apart) around the central axis, since that produces equal grooves and is WRONG. Instead offset them unevenly around the axis (roughly 130/230 degree split, not 180/180) so that, travelling up the image, the two ribbons cross paths at UNEVENLY SPACED points: a SHORT vertical gap to the next crossing (the ribbons stay close together there, a narrow pinched region = minor groove) immediately followed by a LONG vertical gap to the following crossing (the ribbons swing widely apart there = major groove), repeating short-gap, long-gap, short-gap, long-gap all the way up — never evenly-spaced crossings. Cut a small wedge-shaped notch/cutaway near the middle of the helix to reveal one rung's cross-section clearly, showing the paired-base rung meeting each backbone edge-on. CRITICAL RULES: exactly TWO strands (never three or more); the sugar-phosphate backbones are on the OUTSIDE and the paired bases are on the INSIDE meeting at the central axis (never inverted); the two backbones twist in a continuous smooth spiral (never a flat untwisted ladder with straight parallel rails); no uracil, no single-stranded regions, no hairpins or loops (this is plain double-stranded B-DNA, not RNA). Exactly ONE double helix, no duplicates. ABSOLUTELY NO TEXT OF ANY KIND anywhere in the image — no letters (including no 'A', 'T', 'G', 'C' glyphs on or near any rung), no numbers, no words, no scale bars, no arrows, no watermarks. Identify the two rung types purely by their distinct colour pairs, never by any written character.
